                        </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> whom they carried away from thence <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">These words belong, either 1. to both the foregoing branches, and to the <ns0:hi>Israelites;</ns0:hi> and then the sense is, They trod in the steps of their predecessors, the <ns0:hi>Israelites</ns0:hi> (who, in regard of their several Tribes, are both here, and elswhere, called <ns0:hi>Nations</ns0:hi>) who did, many of them, worship both God in their Calves, and <ns0:hi>Baal</ns0:hi> too. Or, 2. to the last branch onely; but then the words must be otherwise rendred; <ns0:hi>they served their own gods, after the manner of the Nations from which they brought,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>carried them,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>from whence they</ns0:hi> (these new Inhabitants) <ns0:hi>were</ns0:hi> brought; <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> each of them served the god of the country or place whence he was brought, as is related above, <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 30, 31. But these Nations could not so pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />perly be said to be <ns0:hi>carried away,</ns0:hi> or to be <ns0:hi>carried away captive</ns0:hi> (as this <ns0:hi>Hebrew</ns0:hi> word signifies), as the <ns0:hi>Israel<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ites;</ns0:hi> and therefore the former interpretation seems more proper.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="34">34 Unto this day they <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">Either 1. the <ns0:hi>Samaritans,</ns0:hi> whose Religion he hath hi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />therto been describing, and to the description whereof he re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />
                        <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                           <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>, <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 41. So the following Verses are a digression, wherein he designs onely to take an occasion to com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pare them with the <ns0:hi>Israelites,</ns0:hi> and to aggravate the sins of the <ns0:hi>Israelites</ns0:hi> above theirs, which he doth, <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 35, &c. and then returns to the former description, <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 31. Or rather, 2. The <ns0:hi>Israelites,</ns0:hi> who are the principal Subjects of this whole Discourse; and of whom he unquestionably speaks, <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 35. and thence to <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 41. of whom also the last words of <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 33. are to be understood; and from thence he takes an occasion to return to his main business, to relate, and aggravate the sins of <ns0:hi>Israel;</ns0:hi> and thereby to justifie his severe proceedings against them, to all the World. So the sense of the place is this; As the <ns0:hi>Israelites</ns0:hi> before their captivity, gave these Nations an ill Example, in serving the Lord, and <ns0:hi>Baal</ns0:hi> together; so, or <ns0:hi>after their former manner, they do unto this day,</ns0:hi> in the land of their captivity.</ns0:note> do after the former manners: they fear not the LORD <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">Though they pretended to fear, and serve both the Lord and Idols, yet in truth they did not, and do not fear or worship the Lord, but their own Calves, or other vain inventions: And God will not accept that mongrel and false Worship, which they pretend to give to the true God. Or, this may intimate, that the <ns0:hi>Israelites</ns0:hi> were worse than their Successors, because these feared the Lord, and Idols too; but they did quite cast off the fear and worship of God in their captivity, and wholly degene<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rated into Heathenish Idolatry.</ns0:note>, neither do they after their statutes <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> God's Law deli<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vered to their Fathers, and to them, as their Inheritance, <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 119. 111. This is alledged as an Evidence, that they did not fear the Lord, whatsoever they pretended, because they lived in the constant breach of his statutes.</ns0:note>, or after their ordinan<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ces, or after the law and commandment which the LORD commanded the children of Jacob <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> Themselves: the Noun put for the Pronoun; which is usual among the <ns0:hi>Hebrews.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note>, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Gen. 32. 28. and 35. 10.</ns0:note> whom he named Israel <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">A Name, signifying his special interest in God, and power with him, which was gi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ven to him, not onely for himself, but for his Posterity also, whom God frequently honours with that Name. And by this great favour he aggravates their sin.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="35">35 With whom the LORD had made a cove<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nant <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">Containing many precious promises, upon the con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dition here following: see <ns0:hi>Gen:</ns0:hi> 17. 7. <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 19. 5. and 24. 7.</ns0:note>, and charged them, saying, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Judg. 6. 10.</ns0:note> Ye shall not fear other gods, nor bow your selves to them, nor serve them, nor sacrifice to them:</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="36">36 But the LORD, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt, with great power, and a stretched-out arm<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> him shall ye fear, him shall ye worship, and to him shall ye do sacrifice.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="37">37 And the statutes, and the ordinances, and the law, and the commandment which he wrote for you, ye shall observe to do for evermore, and ye shall not fear other gods:</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="38">38 And the covenant that I have made with you, ye shall not forget, neither shall ye fear other gods.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="39">39 But the Lord your God <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> God above, as the whole context shews.</ns0:note> ye shall fear, and he shall deliver you out of the hand of all your e<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nemies <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">And therefore you have no pretence of need to go to other gods for relief.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="40">40 Howbeit, they did not hearken, but they did after their former manner.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="41">41 So <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> In like manner, and after their example.</ns0:note> these nations <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">Who came in their stead.</ns0:note> feared the LORD, and served their graven images, both their children, and their childrens children: as did their fathers, so do they unto this day.</ns0:p>
